description: Pulling a CCB group roster could time out and fail with a bare 502 instead of returning anyone. CCB's group data often leaves phone numbers out, so RADIUS was fetching them one person at a time — which takes half a second each and runs past the server's ten-second limit at around eighteen people, smaller than most real groups. Callers can now ask for the roster without the phone numbers and get it back in about a second, then fill the numbers in afterwards through a new endpoint that works in timed batches and hands back whatever it didn't reach. RADIUS's own screens are unchanged — they still get phone numbers the way they always have.

When you paste a list into a campaign, a cell holding several values separated by semicolons — "Hosts; Prayer" in a Team column — was read as a single value, so that person ended up on one team literally named "Hosts; Prayer" instead of showing up under both. It now splits into separate values, so grouping and filtering find them under each one. Commas are deliberately left alone, since campus names contain them ("Flower Mound, North"). This also makes duplicating a pasted-list campaign exact: someone on two teams with no CCB ID used to come back merged into that junk value.

RADIUS can now hand Valley Creek Pulse a CCB form's responses, which is what lets Pulse run its own follow-up campaigns. Pulse holds no CCB credentials of its own — every CCB call it makes comes through RADIUS, so the church's shared 10,000-a-day CCB limit still has exactly one consumer, with one budget guard and one set of telemetry watching it. The existing group roster endpoint can also return the group's name now when asked, so Pulse can roll a campaign up by campus without anyone re-typing group names. Nothing changes for RADIUS itself: campaigns here work exactly as they did.

Marking circles active or inactive in CCB from Mass Update failed for every circle, reporting "Request failed with status code 500" next to each leader's name. RADIUS was sending CCB the change to make but not the circle it applied to, so CCB had nothing to update and rejected the whole write. The circle is now identified the way CCB expects, and the update goes through. RADIUS also reads CCB's reply back to confirm each circle actually landed on the value you picked, and when CCB does reject something it now reports what CCB said instead of a bare error code.

Marking circles active or inactive in CCB from Mass Update failed with a server timeout when more than a couple of circles were selected. Each circle is a separate call out to CCB, and the whole selection was being sent as one request that ran past the time limit -- so the update died with no report, even though some circles had already been changed. Mass Update now sends circles to CCB in small batches, shows its progress as it works through them, and if a batch does fail it tells you exactly how many were updated before it stopped. Re-running is safe: circles already set to the value you picked are left alone.

You can now mark circles active or inactive in Church Community Builder straight from Mass Update. Pick "CCB Circle Status" under the new CCB group in the Field to Update list, choose Active or Inactive, select your leaders, and confirm -- RADIUS updates each circle's group in CCB for you, instead of you opening CCB and editing them one at a time. This one writes to CCB rather than RADIUS, so it's marked in amber and asks you to confirm before it runs, and a leader's RADIUS status is left exactly as it was. Leaders with no CCB circle linked are named up front and skipped, and anything CCB rejects is listed by name afterward so nothing fails quietly.

Submitting a Circle Summary more than once no longer inflates the attendance number in Church Community Builder. Guests you add by hand (people who aren't on your roster) are sent to CCB as a head count, and CCB *adds* that number to the meeting instead of replacing it -- so a resubmission, or an automatic retry after a network hiccup, silently counted those guests a second time. Three walk-ins could end up in CCB as six or nine, while the attendee list and notes looked perfectly correct. The toolkit now reads what CCB already has for that meeting and sends only the difference, so submitting again changes nothing. Roster attendees were never affected -- CCB matches those to real people. If CCB is already carrying more guests than your summary reports, it's flagged for the office to correct, because a head count in CCB can be added to but never lowered through the API.

The Connection Tracker now always reads live circle data. It had been serving a frozen snapshot of the leader list, so renamed leaders kept their old names (circle 597 still read "Cindy Cross" after it became "Deborah Weeger"), newly created circles never appeared at all, and every leader's status stayed stuck at whatever it was when the snapshot was taken. Names, statuses, and new circles now show up as soon as they're saved. Logged connections on a leader's page get the same fix.

The status filter on the Connection Tracker now lists every leader status -- Invited, Pipeline, On-Boarding, Active, Paused, and Off-Boarding -- instead of only the statuses leaders happen to have right now. Previously the dropdown was built from whoever was on the page, so in a season where every leader is paused, Paused was the only choice and you couldn't filter down to your active leaders.

Meetings your Circle actually held now always show up in the Events list, even when they fall outside your usual meeting rhythm. Previously, if a bi-weekly Circle met on an off week, that meeting was hidden from the toolkit (and couldn't be summarized) because it didn't match the expected schedule -- even though attendance was already recorded in Church Community Builder. Now any date with recorded attendance or a submitted summary is shown regardless of cadence, while blank off-week dates stay hidden so the list doesn't fill up with meetings that never happened.

Circle leader profiles now include a Circle Snapshot (ACPD only): pick a timeframe -- last month, 3 months, 6 months, or this semester -- and instantly see the honest numbers for that circle: average attendance and whether it's trending up or down, what percentage of the roster shows up, meetings met vs. skipped, who was added to the roster, new faces and when they first appeared, and who's been showing up consistently. From there, one tap generates an AI coaching summary that reads the whole timeframe's meeting notes and gives you a coaching read: themes in the notes, what to celebrate, what to watch for, and suggested questions for your next conversation. Generated summaries are saved and shared, so other ACPDs see them without re-generating.

Auto Send now has its own home in Settings. The new Auto Send tab checks everything in one place: whether the Mac Companion server is running and up to date, whether the Messages app is ready to send, whether Text Message Forwarding can reach non-iPhone numbers, and whether delivery tracking (Full Disk Access) is on. You can run all the checks with one click, walk through the guided setup, and send yourself a test text that confirms the whole pipeline -- including the delivery receipt. The setup prompts on Bulk Message and Campaigns now point here instead of each carrying their own copy of the wizard.

Deleting a board, list, card, label, or checklist now shows Radius's own confirmation dialog instead of the browser's built-in popup. In some embedded browsers those built-in popups never appeared, which made delete buttons look broken -- clicking Delete did nothing. The new dialog always shows up, matches the app's dark styling, and supports Enter to confirm and Escape to cancel.

Boards can now import people straight from a CCB event. Open the board menu, choose Import from CCB Event, and enter the event's ID -- everyone who checked in is pulled up, one card per person. Want just the newcomers? Add an optional created-after date and only attendees whose CCB profile was created after that date are included. Each card's title is the person's name, and the description includes the event they attended (with the day they showed up), their phone and email (so the Call, Text, and Email buttons work right away), and when their profile was created. Before importing you choose which list the cards land on and can tag them all with an existing label or create a new one on the spot.

The Mass Update tool's Status dropdown now lists every leader status, including Pipeline and Archived. Previously it only offered a fixed subset, so you couldn't mass-archive circles or move a batch of leaders into the Pipeline status.

The Circle Summary submit button now shows a radiating circle animation while your submission is being sent. The expanding circles give visual feedback that something is happening and reinforce the app's identity.

Submitting a Circle Summary now double-checks that it actually landed in Church Community Builder before showing success. Previously, CCB could occasionally accept a submission and quietly drop it -- the toolkit said it worked, but the summary never appeared in CCB. Now the toolkit reads the summary back from CCB right after saving; if it isn't there, it automatically saves it a second time, and if CCB still doesn't have it you'll see a clear message asking you to tap Submit Again -- with everything you typed kept in place, so nothing needs to be re-entered. Connection drops get the same treatment: your answers stay put and the button simply becomes Submit Again.

The Circles Toolkit is quicker to open and move around in. Tapping Submit on a summary no longer waits on an extra Church Community Builder lookup it never used, the Roster tab stops re-downloading the list it just showed you, and switching back to the app from another app no longer re-runs the whole alert check every time. The red needs summary dot on the Events tab is now counted from data already on hand instead of a fresh CCB call, so it can lag by a few minutes in one specific case: a summary entered directly in CCB rather than in the toolkit. Summaries submitted in the toolkit still clear it instantly, and opening the Events tab always shows the live, authoritative list. Separately, actions like saving a draft, searching for a member, or submitting a summary were each quietly making two trips to the server instead of one -- now they make one.

The Status and ACPD filters on Find a Circle now let you pick more than one at a time. Check off any combination -- Active and Paused, or two ACPDs -- and each one shows as a removable chip in the field. Pick All Statuses or All ACPDs to clear them.

Text or call a person straight from their card on a campaign. The Text button opens Messages with the campaign message already filled in for them -- the same one-tap outreach as a leader's profile page -- and after you send, a one-tap Mark contacted logs it without opening the bulk Follow Up flow.
